page: Hetzner Cloud cax31 is an arm64-based virtual server powered by the Ampere Altra processor family using Neoverse-N1 cores. It features 8 shared vCPUs (8 physical cores) running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 160 GB local NVMe SSD. The server operates under a QEMU hypervisor and does not include any dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate average multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 14164.78 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5619.0. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 1029.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1779.08. Memory bandwidth is solid for cached operations, reaching 553.72 GB/sec for small blocks, but drops to 75.87 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 32.14 GB/sec for writes. Database operations and web serving show moderate capability, with PassMark database operations scoring 5283.78 and static web serving throughput reaching 7.92 GB/sec. Redis SET operations perform at 9.74 million operations per second.

The cax31 server offers a resource-dense, budget-friendly hardware profile utilizing shared ARM64 cores. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under sustained workloads, alongside weak single-core execution speeds and poor performance in complex tasks like 7B LLM text generation. However, the inclusion of 160 GB of fast NVMe SSD storage and a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads. It is best suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight database operations that benefit from parallel physical cores without requiring dedicated CPU execution.
